messages.text:
A couple of parser edge cases surfaced under probing: Clap reports canonical long option names when a value is missing, and repeated single-value options are rejected instead of taking the last value.

I’m patching that parser behavior so invalid invocations fail before any search starts.

commands.commandLine:
"C:\\Program Files\\PowerShell\\7\\pwsh.exe" -Command "@'
import subprocess,pathlib,json
ref=pathlib.Path('REFERENCE_BINARY.txt').read_text().strip()
for args in [ ['-i','rust-reference/test-files/2.test.txt.zip','-i','rust-reference/test-files/3.test.txt.zip'], ['-i','rust-reference/test-files/2.test.txt.zip','-c','l','-c','d'], ['-i','rust-reference/test-files/2.test.txt.zip','--workers','1','--workers','2']]:
 r=subprocess.run([ref]+args,capture_output=True,text=True,timeout=10)
 print('CASE',args)
 print(json.dumps({'c':r.returncode,'o':r.stdout,'e':r.stderr},ensure_ascii=False))
'@ | python -"
